questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Guinea?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Guinea on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Guinea article.

questions.proof: Guinea borders 6 countries: Guinea-Bissau, Senegal, Mali, Ivory Coast, Liberia, Sierra Leone.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Conakry?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Guinea is Conakry.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Guinea?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Prefectures and regions” part of the Guinea article.

questions.proof: The capital of Guinea, Conakry, is a special area.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Guinea about 245,857 square kilometres; Tunisia about 163,610 square kilometres; Togo about 56,785 square kilometres; The Gambia about 11,300 square kilometres.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Guinea on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Guinea on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
